transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hello, Doctor. Well... I suppose what finally made me come in and say something is that, after I eat too much, I’ve been going upstairs and making myself throw up. And then I just act as if I’m just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed so no one notices. It's just gotten to a point where I realized I needed to talk to someone about it.
When you eat before making yourself throw up, would you say you're eating a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar situation, and do you feel out of control while eating?

Yes, I would say so. When no one is in the kitchen, I can go through a whole lot of food. I'll eat leftovers from a church supper, crackers, cheese, cookies... even whatever I just baked for my book club, all in one sitting. It's far more than I would ever serve myself at a regular meal. And yes, once I start eating like that, I really do feel completely out of control.
How would you describe your current weight compared to what others might expect for someone of your height and build? Do you feel you are at a normal weight, overweight, or underweight?

I would say I'm at a normal weight. I mean, I haven't noticed any major changes, and my clothes still fit the same as they usually do. So, yes, just a normal, average weight for someone my height, I think.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with recurrent binge eating episodes (large quantities of food consumed with loss of control) followed by regular purging behavior (self-induced vomiting) to compensate for binges. She maintains normal weight through purging, which is the defining feature of bulimia nervosa, purging type (F50.02). The binge-purge cycle is deliberate, distressing, and secretive. Onset and frequency criteria for bulimia nervosa are met.

confirmed_symptoms: Consumption of large quantities of food (leftovers, crackers, cheese, cookies, baked goods) in single sittings
Eating far more than would be served at a regular meal
Subjective sense of loss of control during eating episodes
Binge eating occurs when alone in kitchen
Regular self-induced vomiting after binge episodes
Deliberate purging behavior to prevent weight gain
Secretive purging (hiding behavior by pretending to tidy kitchen or get ready for bed)
Maintains normal weight despite binge-purge cycle
Clothes fit the same as usual

additional_requirements: Binge-purge episodes are recurrent and regular
